title: Make the pie bigger
src: Von Neumann and Morgenstern, 1944; Fisher and Ury, Getting to Yes, 1981
idea: Not every negotiation is zero-sum. When people want different things, you can often trade so that both get more.
apply: Before haggling over one number, ask what each side values most, and trade what is cheap for you and valuable to them.
remind: Look for trades that grow the pie.
who: Mina, who asks her boss for a raise in a frozen budget.

scenes.nar: Mina asks her boss for an eight thousand dollar raise. The budget is frozen, so the boss says no, and it looks like a stalemate.

items: Every dollar I win, you lose

scenes.nar: If the only question is how much money, it is zero-sum: every dollar she wins, the company loses.

items.x: Trade: remote Fridays and a training budget

scenes.nar: Mina asks what each side values. The boss cannot spend more, and Mina wants flexibility and growth. So they trade: remote Fridays and a training budget.

items.x: Mina gets what she values most

scenes.nar: The budget stays frozen, Mina gets what she values most, and they plan a pay review in six months. Both end up better off.
